title: Auditor‑Ready Brief: RBACv2 / SIEM Export Evidence Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a compact, auditor-facing playbook that bundles: (1) control-to-evidence mapping for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 as it pertains to RBAC v2 and audit-log exports; (2) prioritized gap analysis with remediation guidance; (3) fast evidence collection strategies using our evidence automation pipeline and SIEM export; and (4) a curated set of Q&A and artifacts to bring to auditor interviews.

High-level summary / scope:
- Scope: RBAC v2 enforcement (policy authoring, role assignment, revocation), audit log schema and retention, SIEM export ingestion and transformation, and automation that ties logs to control evidence bundles.
- Intended audience: external auditor, internal security reviewers, engineering owners (serving-runtime, infra, platform).
- Expected outcome for next auditor meeting: provide clear evidence bundles for 6 controls (Authz change control, Least Privilege, Access Reviews, Log Capture & Integrity, Log Retention, Detection Pipeline) and answer common auditor questions without ad-hoc data pulls.

Approach to control mapping (high level):
We map each control to 3 tiers of evidence: (A) system-generated artifacts (immutable logs, SIEM exports), (B) configuration snapshots (RBAC policies, role manifests, IaC), and (C) process artifacts (review minutes, Jira tickets, ticket approvals). The playbook focuses on producing tier A and B artifacts from automated exports first, with C as lightweight human context.

Example control mappings (abbreviated):
- Control: Authorization change control (SOC2 CC6 / ISO A.9.2)
  Evidence: RBAC v2 change events (audit log event: role.created / role.updated / binding.deleted), PRs merging IaC role changes, ticket ID linkage in log metadata.
- Control: Periodic access reviews (SOC2 CC6.2 / ISO A.9.2.3)
  Evidence: exports from access-review tool, signed review report (PDF), and matching last-changed timestamps in audit logs.
- Control: Immutable log capture and retention (SOC2 CC7 / ISO A.12.4)
  Evidence: SIEM export file (daily), S3 object metadata (write-once tags), retention policy config, and MD5 check values stored in attestations table.

Prioritized gap analysis (quick list):
1) Missing explicit event types for delegated-role-approval flows (severity: medium) — some approval steps are recorded only as ticket transitions, not as explicit audit_log events.
2) Inconsistent ticket-id propagation into RBAC change events (severity: high) — causes difficulty proving change origin.
3) SIEM export transformation loses original event_id field in daily compact format (severity: high) — impacts traceability across ingestion pipeline.
4) Access review artifacts are present but lack sign-off hashes stored with the review PDF (severity: low).

Remediation suggestions (practical):
- Add a lightweight producer change: include ticket_id and actor_email as standard fields on all RBAC change events (owner: platform-engineering, PR: GH link in linked_artifacts). Target: 2-week dev cycle.
- Patch SIEM export transformer to preserve original event_id and event_timestamp in compact exports. Add a regression test to run in CI. Owner: observability.
- Introduce an approval step emitter in the change workflow: when an approval completes in Zendesk/Jira, emit an approval.event to audit log. Owner: solutions-engineering and infra.
- Bake review sign-off hash into the review PDF metadata and add a registry record in compliance DB. Owner: security-and-compliance.

Evidence automation plan (how to assemble auditor bundles):
1) Query SIEM daily compact exports for the audit period. Pull objects for the date range and validate MD5 checks against manifest in S3.
2) Use the evidence-assembler lambda (runbook: runbook:siem-export-validation-v1) to correlate RBAC events by event_id to PRs and Jira keys via the ticket_id field.
3) Produce a signed ZIP per control that includes: raw-export.jsonl (subset), transformation manifest, config snapshots (RBAC policy YAML), and a short human-readable rationale (1 page).
4) Store signed bundles to the auditor-share bucket with object ACL configured for read-only auditor links.

SIEM export validation checklist (pre-audit run):
- Ensure exporter version >= v2.1.3 (contains event_id preservation).
- Run schema validator against sample exports (schema: auditlog_v3).
- Confirm all RBAC change events include fields: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, ticket_id, role_id, change_type, source_ip, request_id.
- Verify retention settings: objects exist for required retention window (SOC2: min 180 days; ISO: per contract/regulatory needs).
- Compare event counts against system counters (RBAC metrics) to detect missing batches.

RBAC v2 audit-log schema snippet (plain text example to include in evidence):
- event_id: string (UUIDv4)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- actor_id: string (internal user id)
- actor_email: string
- ticket_id: string (JIRA-####)
- role_id: string
- change_type: enum [create, update, delete, bind, unbind]
- details: free-text summary (max 2048 chars)
- request_id: string (trace id)
- source_ip: string
- signature: string (optional HMAC over event payload)

Auditor Q&A (selected anticipated questions and suggested responses):
Q: How do you prove who approved a role change?
A: Provide the event sequence: role.change request (ticket_id present) -> approval.event (audit log with approver actor_email and timestamp) -> role.assigned event. Correlate with PR that changed IaC (PR id in details). We produce a zipped bundle showing these three artifacts.

Q: What prevents log tampering?
A: Logs are written to WORM-enabled S3 bucket, SIEM ingestion runs under dedicated service account. Each daily export has an MD5 manifest and a publish attest record signed by our compliance key. For high-sensitivity events, we include HMAC signatures at event level.

Q: Can you show access review evidence for the past 6 months?
A: Yes — automated exports of review reports (PDF) with embedded sign-off hash and a registry entry linking to reviewer identities and timestamps. We also include last-modified timestamps in RBAC policies to prove there were no changes post-review.

Meeting / handoff checklist (for the auditor session):
- Pre-upload bundles for the requested date range to auditor-share.
- Send auditor short index (CSV) with sample event ids and ticket ids for spot checks.
- Prepare 3-minute demo: run a trace from event_id -> commit -> PR -> ticket.
- Prepare answers for the Q&A above and have platform engineers on standby.

Open questions and risks: 
- We still need to finalize the HMAC key rotation policy for event-level signatures (assigned to security ops).
- Automation coverage does not yet include delegated approvals via third-party identity providers (small subset of orgs) — risk: missing explicit approval.events.

Acceptance criteria for auditor-ready bundle: 
- Contains at least one complete trace per control demonstrating origin -> approval -> execution.
- SIEM exports validate against schema and MD5 manifest.
- All RBAC events include ticket_id or a documented reason for missing ticket_id.

Next steps / action items (owners and ETA):
- Platform: ticket_id standardization in RBAC events (Ethan Li) — ETA: 2026-03-01.
- Observability: fix transformer to preserve event_id (Marisa Clark) — ETA: 2026-02-28 (in QA).
- Security: finalize event HMAC rotation policy (Priya Menon) — ETA: 2026-03-10.
- Compliance: run a dry-run evidence assembly and produce three control bundles (Daniel Becker) — ETA: 2026-03-05.

Notes to self / draft markers: 
- Keep playbook pragmatic: auditors want traceability, not perfect telemetry. Focus on reproducible traces.
- Record any auditor follow-ups as JIRA tickets and surface in the next revision of this document.

End of brief.
